topicTitle: Clausius and Kelvin Statements of the Second Law

questions.prompt: Using the model for Clausius and Kelvin Statements of the Second Law, set up the governing equation, inequality, derivative, probability, or phase-rule count and solve the following problem: A refrigerator removes \(Q_C=600\,\mathrm{J}\) from its cold compartment and rejects \(Q_H=750\,\mathrm{J}\) to the room in one cycle. Find the required work and explain why the device satisfies the Clausius statement.
questions.answer:
Model:
Apply the model for Clausius and Kelvin Statements of the Second Law under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Working:
Apply the cyclic energy balance in equation \([1]\): \[W_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_H-Q_C=750\,\mathrm{J}-600\,\mathrm{J}=150\,\mathrm{J}.\] The device transfers heat from cold to hot, but that transfer is not its sole result because \(150\,\mathrm{J}\) of work is supplied. The signs and units also verify \(750=600+150\). Final result: \(W_{\mathrm{in}}=150\,\mathrm{J}\), so the refrigerator does not violate the Clausius statement.

Final answer:
\(W_{\mathrm{in}}=150\,\mathrm{J}\), so the refrigerator does not violate the Clausius statement.

Check:
Substituting the result back into the defining relation reproduces the stated data to the quoted precision. The final unit follows from the equation, and the qualitative trend agrees with the model.
